riley: quick heads-up / gryphon-v4q-int4 canary showing a small but visible bump in funcall JSON parse failures, almost exclusively on streaming path when prompts include code fences.

chen: numbers? reproducible?

riley: from our nightly 2k sample: fp16 0.12% parse_fail, int8 0.18%, int4 1.7%. repro rate higher when kv_prefix_trim=true and batch_size>1.

omar: paste an example please

riley: hereraw reassembled stream (exact order):

```
system: Respond only with JSON
Assistant: ok generating
{
  "action": "run_tests",
  "args": {
    "cases": [
      {"name": "edge", "script": "```\ndef foo():\n  return 1\n```"}
    ]
  }
}
BUILD-META: id=71a2

```

riley: sometimes the code fence causes an extra ``` token that shifts chunk boundaries; when a post-JSON footer is flushed concurrently the footer can appear before the final chunk with closing brace arrives. net: truncated JSON or footer injected mid-structure.

chen: seems like a race: async footer flush vs model chunk order. build-bot: detected recent change to logging flush (PR #1892) that could flip end-of-stream ordering.

build-bot: flagged PR #1892 as potential cause.

omar: mitigation idea: reassembler should treat any chunk that matches /^BUILD-META:/ as metadata and buffer it until we've seen a valid complete JSON parse. if parse fails after repair attempts, then emit metadata. simple heuristic: only drop post-EOF metadata if it arrives within 200ms of a closing brace.

riley: I prototyped a sanitizer: strip lines matching /^(BUILD-META:|Response-ID:)/ and trim leading/trailing non-json bytes before strict parse; results: parse_fail -> 0.4% on canary.

chen: good short-term. long-term options: 1) revert async logging flush (infra), 2) add chunk sequence numbers to stream protocol (runtime), 3) teach model to avoid emitting code fence tokens at boundary (model team).

omar: also add an eval check in onboarding: run the structured-output testset with streaming+kv_trim for every quantized candidate and assert parse_fail <0.5% or repairs<0.5% separately. log repairs as separate metric.

ana: created tickets LOG-918 (revert flush), RUNTIME-458 (chunk-seq), EVAL-1333 (streaming-quant-onboard test).

riley: rolling sanitizer to canary tonight (01:30 UTC) with debug chunk seq logging. will report back with 12h snapshot.

chen: if sanitizer looks safe, we should expose it as opt-out SDK parse flag for hosted customers.

riley: agreed. linking tickets in this thread. thanks.
